cohort: This study included 27 pregnancies in 18 women with severe antithrombin deficiency (antithrombin level of <0.55 IU/ml with or without prior venous thromboembolism, or an antithrombin level < 0.8 IU/ml and a personal history of venous thromboembolism).
finding: High doses of low molecular weight heparin are needed to achieve therapeutic anti-activated factor X levels in pregnant women with severe antithrombin deficiency, but this approach is associated with a high rate of live births.
